agency_name: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (NCDEQ)
mission: Providing science-based environmental stewardship for the health and prosperity of all North Carolinians.
user: The NCDEQ grants coordinator, who watches federal funding notices for the department, decides which are worth pursuing, and routes each one to the division that would own the application.

strategic_priorities.name: Environmental and Public Health Protection
strategic_priorities.description: Protect public health by setting and implementing science-based standards and by providing technical, compliance, permitting and financial assistance to residents, communities, businesses, and local governments to meet or exceed requirements, prevent pollution, and improve public health.

objectives.text: Sustain and enhance water quality: water supply planning, invest state and federal water infrastructure funding in drinking water and wastewater projects for communities with the greatest need, manage pathogens, toxins and nutrients, and improve stormwater compliance.
Protect outdoor, ambient air quality: air quality monitoring for hazardous and criteria pollutants, air permits, and compliance through inspections and technical assistance.
Preserve and enhance land quality: brownfields redevelopment, assessment and remediation of solid waste, hazardous waste and Superfund sites, waste reduction and recovery, and dam safety.
Protect coastal resources and marine life: coastal habitat and fisheries management plans, watershed restoration with nature-based solutions, and enforcement in coastal waters.

Promote environmental stewardship and sustainable practices among businesses and local governments through compliance and pollution prevention assistance, natural resource conservation and recycling programs.

strategic_priorities.name: Community Restoration and Resilience
strategic_priorities.description: Support and accelerate the long-term recovery of communities devastated by Hurricane Helene and other natural disasters, and lead state efforts to strengthen communities' resiliency to future disasters.

objectives.text: Coordinate with state and local government on resilience partnerships and integrate data and science into grant programs and community projects.
Support communities' efforts to build resilience to natural hazards and increasingly extreme weather and integrate resilience into long-term recovery.
Support community flood resilience planning and projects using the North Carolina Flood Resiliency Blueprint across river basins.
Use department resources to reduce the impacts of natural hazards such as flooding, landslides and dam breaches, and administer resilience grants directly to communities.

strategic_priorities.name: Forever Chemicals (PFAS)
strategic_priorities.description: Protect North Carolina's people and natural resources from exposure to PFAS and other forever chemicals, using a transparent, collaborative, and science-based decision-making process.

objectives.text: Identify communities at risk of PFAS exposure, test private wells and provide alternate drinking water, reduce PFAS discharges, and expand scientific knowledge of PFAS health risks.
Protect drinking water through science-based PFAS monitoring, reporting and pollution prevention requirements and technical assistance.
Clean up existing PFAS contamination by remediating known sites that impact communities.
Communicate with and educate impacted communities and partners about forever chemicals.

strategic_priorities.name: Environmental Infrastructure
strategic_priorities.description: Strengthen North Carolina's infrastructure through thoughtful and strategic investments.

objectives.text: Use a unified approach across programs for infrastructure funding, in partnership with local governments and universities.
Administer funding and programs for reliable, resilient and viable environmental infrastructure such as drinking water, wastewater and stormwater systems.
Help utilities plan viable infrastructure, with a focus on distressed local government units, and make communities aware of infrastructure funding.
Use federal and state funding efficiently for Hurricane Helene recovery and other disaster recovery, with technical assistance to grantees.

strategic_priorities.name: Community Engagement and Public Participation
strategic_priorities.description: Ensure the meaningful involvement and fair treatment of all people with respect to the development, implementation, and enforcement of environmental laws, health safeguards, and policies.

objectives.text: Make funding processes transparent and understandable to all communities, and alert residents and businesses to state and federal grant opportunities.
Inform stakeholders about regulatory programs, provide community-level information and language access, and increase public participation.
Encourage stakeholder engagement on issues of concern to economically disadvantaged communities.

strategic_priorities.name: Modernize DEQ
strategic_priorities.description: Modernize processes and foster innovation to enhance efficiency in services, increase transparency, and strengthen partnerships to better serve all stakeholders and the general public.

objectives.text: Modernize permit, compliance and inspection processes and reduce permit backlogs.
Develop secure digital solutions, cyber security, and explore artificial intelligence for agency business.
Enhance technical assistance and regional office support for permit applicants, businesses and the public.

strategic_priorities.name: Work Environment
strategic_priorities.description: Create a work environment where employees feel valued and are empowered to be active participants in developing science-based solutions to better protect public health and the environment.

objectives.text: Foster creativity, collaboration and joint research projects with academia and external partners.
Provide professional development, career pathways and recruitment for environmental workforce.
Cultivate leadership, mentoring and teamwork across divisions.

divisions.name: Division of Air Quality

divisions.name: Division of Water Resources

divisions.name: Division of Water Infrastructure
divisions.scope: drinking water and clean water state revolving funds, wastewater and stormwater infrastructure grants and loans, lead service lines, viable utilities

divisions.name: Division of Waste Management
divisions.scope: solid and hazardous waste, Superfund, brownfields, underground storage tanks, PFAS remediation

divisions.name: Division of Energy, Mineral and Land Resources
divisions.scope: stormwater permits, erosion and sediment control, dam safety, mining, geological survey

divisions.name: Division of Coastal Management
divisions.scope: coastal zone management, coastal resilience, estuarine reserves, coastal permits

divisions.name: Division of Marine Fisheries
divisions.scope: marine and estuarine fisheries management, habitat protection, fisheries enforcement

divisions.name: Division of Environmental Assistance and Customer Service
divisions.scope: pollution prevention, recycling and waste reduction, environmental stewardship, permit assistance

divisions.name: State Energy Office
divisions.scope: energy efficiency, clean energy, weatherization and energy programs

divisions.name: Division of Mitigation Services
divisions.scope: stream and wetland restoration, watershed mitigation

divisions.name: Office of the Secretary and central administration
divisions.scope: resilience coordination, PFAS science, community engagement, digital services, workforce, federal funds
